text:
ani: Heads up — EU2 GPU pool failing to join after firewall hardening. ~20% of nodes time out during bootstrap. Seeing KMS AccessDenied in the node logs.

tom: Ugh, which KMS key/grant? Any log lines?

ani: Paste from node bootstrap: 
```
2026-03-23T10:12:03Z ERROR bootstrap: failed to decrypt /etc/keystore: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/gpu-node-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01
Caused by: grant not found or expired
```

selma: Firewall hardening rolled out earlier today tightened egress to only allow privatelink endpoints and blocked direct S3/KMS endpoints. The audit-shipper service (delivers instance audit logs to our SIEM) still uses a NAT path to S3 and the keystore grant lifetime is short — nodes are failing while waiting on the shipper ack, grant expires.

ops-sre: Quick proposal: create a temporary allowlist rule for the audit shipper and the KMS endpoints from the GPU subnets so keystore decrypts succeed during onboarding. Then we can change the shipper to use privatelink or an STS-assume-role flow. Who can own the allowlist change?

ani: I can own the change, but need approval from security/compliance. Compliance: we can restrict allowlist to only the audit-shipper ENIs + KMS SNI, TTL 2 hours, logged.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-1045 - "eu2 gpu onboarding KMS AccessDenied after egress lockdown". Pager duty: @ops-sre paging.

tom: Cost/controls note: keeping NAT egress open even briefly will increase S3 egress and audit traffic visibility. If we do this, add detailed packet-logging and set a strict TTL. Also consider short-lived delegated grant instead of opening wide egress.

selma: We can add a delegated KMS grant during bootstrap from control-plane: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/gpu-keystore --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/gpu-node-role --operations Decrypt --retiring-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/control-plane --name onboarding-grant-temp
```
That avoids changing firewall rules but requires the control-plane to create the grant before node attempts decrypt. Might be faster and safer.

ops-sre: Both paths workable. Tradeoffs:
- Temp grant: low-network blast radius, requires control-plane change and quick sequencing.
- Allowlist: fastest (ani can push now) but wider network exposure for TTL.

ani: Compliance responded in DM: temporary allowlist OK for 30 minutes if logged; longer needs service owner signoff. They want evidence that audit logs still delivered.

ops-sre: Plan: I'll push an allowlist for 30 minutes scoped to audit shipper ENIs + KMS FQDNs from the GPU subnets, enable flow-logs to a locked S3 bucket, and watch node join rate. If green after 20m, extend to 2h while selma implements the create-grant flow as fallback.

tom: Please also annotate the canary with a tag: provisioning:canary=true and route traces to /debug/provisioning so we can measure boot success + time-to-decrypt. Postmortem action: add an e2e check that verifies KMS decrypt path reachable before marking pool healthy.

ani: Pushing patch to firewall now, will post the rule IDs.

ops-sre: Rule IDs: FW-1872 (egress allow audit-shipper ENIs), FW-1873 (egress allow kms.svc.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com). Monitoring: if join failures >5% in 10m revert.

selma: I'll start wiring the control-plane to create the temporary grant and add unit test for grant lifecycle. ETA 90m.

ani: Thanks — nodes are trickling in already. Will update with last join metrics in 15m. :thumbsup:
